summary: Kickoff for Summit Health onboarding to Redwood Dedicated/private deployment. Covered timelines, security and compliance needs (SOC2, KMS, SSO), integration points (VPC, S3), initial pilot scope (chat + embeddings), and success criteria. Agreed next steps: share onboarding plan, schedule technical deep dive, provide staging access, and weekly check-ins.
topics: Security and compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO
Pilot scope: chat + embeddings, throughput targets
Integration points: S3, API keys, RBAC
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Mitchell: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me are Liam Chen, our solutions engineer, and Sofia Patel who's your CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Erica Gomez: Good, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: Hey all. We have a lot to cover, want to make sure we align on timeline and security up front.
[00:15] Ava Mitchell: Yeah totally, quick agenda, 1) confirm scope of pilot and success criteria, 2) go over deployment options — looks like you're leaning private with VPC and some on-prem constraints, 3) security/compliance checklist, 4) timeline and next steps. If that's good we'll jump in.
[00:30] Dr. Erica Gomez: Sounds good. From Summit side, our goals are to integrate a conversational assistant into our provider portal and to embed semantic search over clinical notes. Primary concerns are PHI handling, latency under 300ms for the chat happy path, and cost predictability.
[00:46] Liam Chen: Great, that maps well to our Redwood Dedicated or Private offering; Dedicated gives reserved capacity on our infra, Private is where you run our control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For PHI and compliance you mentioned, most enterprise customers pick Private with customer-managed KMS.
[00:59] Tom Alvarez: Right we have strict KMS policy, and we need audit logs forwarded into our SIEM, and SSO via SAML OKTA. Also we'll need an answer on data residency — all data should stay in us-east-1 for now.
[01:15] Ava Mitchell: All doable. We support KMS/HSM integrations, audit log forwarding, and SAML SSO. We'll include the details in the security pack. Slight note: when you pick Private there are two modes — VPC-hosted control plane vs fully on-prem package. Liam, can you walk high-level architecture?
[01:33] Liam Chen: Sure. At a high level, control plane components run in the customer's VPC and talk to our lightweight agent that schedules model inference. For the inference workload itself you can choose our dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 or we can run in your on-prem infra if you provide the instances. Typical setup: VPC peering to our serving layer, private endpoints for API, KMS for key wrapping, S3 access for model artifacts with fine-grained IAM roles.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: We want the inference to actually run inside our cluster if possible, we have NVIDIA A100s. Latency's critical — can Redwood run inside our network?
[02:07] Liam Chen: Yes, that's our private on-prem option. We'll need to validate kernel compatibility and quantization profiles — sometimes model tuning is required to hit latency targets. We'll plan a benchmark run with a sample model.
[02:22] Dr. Erica Gomez: Benchmarking is key. We'll provide a representative traffic profile — mostly short chats but some longer note summarizations.
[02:29] Ava Mitchell: Great, Marcus can you confirm the traffic profile and sample data by next Wednesday?
[02:33] Marcus Lee: Yep, I'll get that over by 2027-03-23.
[02:36] Tom Alvarez: On security questionnaire — we'll need to validate SOC2 status and encryption at rest, in transit, plus key rotation policy. Also need to review retention settings for logs and PII redaction.
[02:49] Sofia Patel: We can send our security pack, it includes SOC2 report, encryption details, and our logging/audit recommendations. We also support configurable retention and can add PII redaction rules at the ingestion layer.
[03:00] Dr. Erica Gomez: How about SSO? We use Okta and want RBAC so engineers can't access prod keys.
[03:06] Liam Chen: We support SAML SSO via Okta. RBAC maps to roles in the console — you can limit model deployment and key management to specific groups. We'll include an example mapping.
[03:16] Marcus Lee: On the integration side, what does the API look like for chat and embeddings? We want a streaming endpoint for chat and a batched embeddings endpoint for ingest.
[03:25] Liam Chen: APIs are REST/SDK. Streaming uses chunked responses with token-level events; embeddings support bulk upload and batching. For throughput, we recommend configuring batching and prefix caching; we'll show configs based on your profile.
[03:39] Ava Mitchell: For cost predictability, we can propose reserved capacity pricing and an autoscale policy. You mentioned tight latency — reserved capacity with local GPUs will give most consistent performance.
[03:49] Dr. Erica Gomez: What's typical cost delta between hosted and private on-prem?
[03:54] Ava Mitchell: Hosted is generally lower ops for you but can be higher per token; private on-prem shifts infra costs to you, Redwood charges a platform fee and optionally a per-instance runtime license. We'll include a sample TCO in the onboarding deck.
[04:07] Tom Alvarez: We'll need contractual SLAs around uptime and incident response.
[04:11] Ava Mitchell: That's part of the enterprise package; we'll surface SLA options in the quote.
[04:15] Marcus Lee: On rollout plan — we want a canary first in staging, then prod, with metrics gating. Who owns the rollout?
[04:23] Sofia Patel: CSM will coordinate the rollout with your eng and we'll handle runbooks for canary, rollback, and monitoring. We'll set up dashboards for latency/cost per route and alerts if quality regressions appear.
[04:37] Dr. Erica Gomez: For success criteria: 1) deployment in staging with OKTA SSO and KMS integrated; 2) chat latency median <300ms at 95th perc under pilot load; 3) embedding recall above our baseline. If those are met, we'll expand to 50k monthly queries.
[04:59] Ava Mitchell: Perfect. Let's capture next steps: I'll send the onboarding plan and pricing, Liam will schedule the technical deep dive to validate on-prem infra and benchmarking, Marcus will provide staging creds and traffic profile, Tom will share security questionnaire items, Sofia will set up weekly check-ins.
[05:15] Marcus Lee: Good. One quick question — model versions. We want predictable model pinning for regulatory traceability.
[05:21] Liam Chen: We support model version pinning and rollout tags, plus an audit trail for each request that records model and kernel versions.
[05:30] Tom Alvarez: And logs to SIEM?
[05:33] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can forward JSON-formatted audit logs to your SIEM endpoint.
[05:38] Dr. Erica Gomez: Anything else?
[05:40] Ava Mitchell: That's about it. We'll follow up with the deck and schedule invites. Thanks everyone.
[05:45] Dr. Erica Gomez: Thanks. Looking forward to the deep dive.
[05:47] Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
[05:49] End of recording
